output.name: Holtha — the Shore-Waiter
output.myth: When Aun cut the string he was in a hurry, and he left his hound on the shore below the cliffs. Holtha was grey, and his teeth rang like bells when he shook his head. One season he ran the ebb, nose down in the wet weed, hunting his master's smell. Westward the Oilskin Coat kept the spray off its shoulders, and Holtha ran at its edge and never caught it. When the tide turned he barked at every boat that came in late, so crews learned to row hard. Hesk kept count of the boats he turned home. Tavo tried once to blow him off the rocks, but Holtha only shook his coat and ran on. Kael casts for him and has never got him in the net. The old women say: hear bells under the water after dark, row fast and call your own name, knot by knot as the Name-Kite does, so the hound knows you are not Aun. He is up in the Leeward Reach, a grey lamp with his nose to the wind, waiting for a boat that is late.
output.finding: From the Name-Kite, which lies about 16° north of it, look straight south for four-fifths of a hand-span and you will find Holtha, a grey lamp low in the Leeward Reach.
